source_text: Quibus duobus dominis neget posse seruiri, quia alterum offendi sit necesse alterum defendi, ipse declarat, deum proponens et mamonam. proinde mamonam quem intellegi uelit, si interpretem non habes, ab ipso potes discere. admonens enim nos de saecularibus suffragia nobis prospicere amicitiarum secundum serui illius exemplum, qui ab actu summotus dominicos debitores diminutis cautionibus releuat in subsidium sibi: et ego, inquit, dico uobis, facite uobis amicos de mamona iniustitiae, de nummo scilicet, de \' quo et seruus ille. iniustitiae enim auctorem et dominatorem totius saeculi nummum scimus omnes. cui famulatam uidens Pharisaeorum cupiditatem ammentauit hanc sententiam: non potestis deo seruire et mamonae. inridebant denique Pharisaei pecuniae cupidi, quod intellexissent scilicet mamonam de nummo dictum, ne quia existimet in mamona creatorem intellegendum et Christum a creatoris illos seruitute reuocasse.. quid nunc? potius ex hoc disce unum a Christo deum ostensum. duos enim dominos nominauit, deum et mamonam, crea. torem et nummum: denique non potestis deo seruire, utique ei, cui uidebantur seruire, et mamonam, cui magis destinabantur. quodsi ipse alium se ageret, non duos dominos, sed tres demonstrasset — et creator enim dominus, quia deus, et utique magis dominus quam mamonas magisque homini obseruandus, qua magis dominus —; quale est enim, ut qui mamonam dominum dixerat et cum domino iunxerat uero, ipsum dominum taceret, id est deum creatorem? aut numquid tacendo eo concessit seruiendum ei esse, si solummodo sibi et mamonae negauit posse seruiri? ita cum unum deum ponit, nominaturus et creatorem, si alius esset ipse, creatorem nominauit quem [dominum] sine alio [deo non] posuit. et illud itaque relucebit, quomodo dictum sit: (si) in mamona iniusto fideles non extitistis, quod uerum est quis uobis credet? in nummo scilicet iniusto, non in creatore, quem et Marcion iustum facit, et: si in alieno fideles inuenti non estis, meum quis dabit uobis? alienum enim debet esse a semis dei quod iniustum est. creator autem quomodo alienus erat Pharisaeis, proprius deus Iudaicae gentis? si ergo haec non cadunt in creatorem, sed in mamonam, \'quis uobis credet quod uerius est\'? et \'quis uobis dabit quod meum est\'? non potest quasi ali{en)us dixisse de alterius dei gratia. tunc enim uideretur ita dixisse, si eos in creatorem, non in mamonam infideles notando per creatoris mentionem distinctione se fecisset dei alterius, non commissuri suam ueritatem infidelibus creatoris, t quoniam tunc alterius uideri potest, si non ad hoc proponatur, ut a re, de qua agitur, separetur. Si autem et iustificantes se coram hominibus Pharisaei spem mercedis in homine ponebant, illo eos sensu increpabat, quo et propheta Hieremias: miser homo, qui spem habet in homine. si et adicit: scit autem deus corda uestra, illius dei uim commemorabat, (qui) lucernam se pronuntiarat scrutantem renes et corda. si superbiam tangit: quod elatum est apud homines perosum est deo, Esaiam ponit ante oculos: dies enim domini Sabaoth in omnem contumeliosum et superbum, in omnem sublimem et elatum, et humiliabuntur. Possum iam colligere, cur tanto aeuo deus Marcionis fuerit in occulto. expectabat, opinor, donec haec omnia disceret a creatore. didicit igitur usque ad Iohannis tempora atque ita exinde processit adnuntiare regnum dei dicens: lex et prophetae usque ad Iohannem; ex quo regnum dei adnuntiatur. quasi non et nos limitem quendam agnoscamus Iohannem constitutum inter uetera et noua, ad quem desineret Iudaismus et a quo inciperet Christianismus, non tamen, ut ab alia uirtute facta sit sedatio legis et prophetarum et initiatio euangelii, in quo est dei regnum.\' [Christus ipse.] nam id si probauimus, et uetera transitura et noua successura praedicari a creatore, si et Iohannes antecursor et praeparator ostenditur uiarum domini euangelium\', superducturi et regnum dei promulgaturi, et ex hoc iam, quod Iohannes uenit, ipse erit Christus qui Iohannem erit subsecutus ut antecursorem; et, si desierunt uetera et coeperunt ! noua interstite Iohanne, non erit mirum quod ex dispositione est creatoris, ut unde(unde) magis probetur ** quam ex legis et prophetarum in Iohannem occasu et exinde ortu regni dei. transeat igitur caelum et terra citius, sicut et lex et: prophetae, quam unus apexuerborum domini-nerbum enim, inquit Esaias, dei nostri manet in aeuum —: nam quoniam in Esaia iam tunc Christus, sermo scilicet et spiritus creatoris, Iohannem praedicarat — uocem clamantis in deserto: parate uiam domini — in hoc uenturum, ut legis et] prophetarum ordo exinde cessaret, per adimpletionem, non per destructionem, et regnum dei a Christo adnuntiaretur, I ideo subtexuit facilius elementa transitura quam uerba sua,\' confirmans hoc quoque, quod de Iohanne dixerat, non praeterisse.
pass_a_gloss: To whom He says that two lords cannot be served, because it is necessary that one offend the other, and defend the other, He Himself declares, setting forth God and mammon. Therefore, mammon, which He wishes to be understood, if you do not have an interpreter, you can learn from Him Himself. For, admonishing us to look out for worldly friendships according to the example of that servant, who, having been removed from office, relieves his master's debtors by diminishing their securities for his own benefit: and I, He says, tell you, make friends for yourselves from the mammon of unrighteousness, from money, of course, from which also that servant. For we all know that money is the author and ruler of all worldly things. Seeing the covetousness of the Pharisees, He strengthened this statement: you cannot serve God and mammon. Finally, the Pharisees, who were greedy for money, ridiculed, because they understood, of course, that mammon was spoken of in terms of money, not because they thought that the creator should be understood in mammon, and that Christ had recalled them from the service of the creator. What now? Rather, learn from this that one God is shown by Christ. For He named two lords, God and mammon, the creator and money: finally, you cannot serve God, certainly to Him, whom they seemed to serve, and mammon, to whom they were more devoted. But if He Himself were acting as another, He would have demonstrated not two lords, but three — and the creator is indeed the Lord, because He is God, and certainly a greater Lord than mammon, and more to be obeyed by man, because He is a greater Lord —; what kind of thing is it, that He who said mammon was Lord and joined it with the true Lord, would be silent about the Lord Himself, that is, the creator God? Or did He, by being silent about it, concede that it should be served, if only He denied that it could be served along with mammon? Thus, when He sets forth one God, He names the creator, if He Himself were another, He named the creator, whom He set forth as Lord without another God. And that statement will also become clear, how it was said: if you have not been faithful in the mammon of unrighteousness, who will trust you? Certainly, in the unjust money, not in the creator, whom even Marcion makes just, and: if you have not been faithful in what is another's, who will give you what is mine? For what is unjust should certainly be alien to the semi-god. But how was the creator alien to the Pharisees, when He was the proper God of the Jewish people? If, therefore, these things do not fall upon the creator, but upon mammon, who will trust you, which is truer? And who will give you what is mine? He cannot have said this as if it were alien, concerning the grace of another God. For then He would seem to have said this, if He had noted them as unfaithful in the creator, not in mammon, by mentioning the creator, making a distinction, so that they would not commit their truth to the unfaithful creator. But if the Pharisees, justifying themselves before men, were putting their hope of reward in men, He was rebuking them with the same sense in which the prophet Jeremiah said: woe to the man who puts his hope in man. And if He adds: but God knows your hearts, He was commemorating the power of that God, who had declared Himself to be the searcher of kidneys and hearts. If He touches on pride: what is exalted among men is an abomination to God, He sets Isaiah before their eyes: for the day of the Lord of hosts will be upon every arrogant and haughty one, and they will be humbled. I can now gather why the God of Marcion was in hiding for so long. He was waiting, I think, until all these things were learned from the creator. Therefore, He learned up to the time of John, and from then on, He proceeded to announce the kingdom of God, saying: the law and the prophets were until John; from whom the kingdom of God is announced. As if we do not recognize a certain boundary established by John between the old and the new, at which Judaism ceased and Christianity began, not, however, that the cessation of the law and the prophets, and the initiation of the gospel, in which is the kingdom of God, was made by another virtue. For if we have proven this, that the old things are passing away and the new things are succeeding, as predicted by the creator, and John is shown to be the forerunner and preparer of the ways of the Lord, and the gospel, which will bring and proclaim the kingdom of God, and from this, now that John has come, He Himself will be Christ, who will follow John as a forerunner; and if the old things have ceased and the new things have begun, with John in between, it will not be surprising that this is from the disposition of the creator, so that it may be proven more than from the passing away of the law and the prophets in John, and from then on, the rising of the kingdom of God. Therefore, let heaven and earth pass away more quickly, just as the law and the prophets, than one dot of the Lord's words — for the word of our God remains forever —; for since in Isaiah, Christ, namely the word and spirit of the creator, had already predicted John, saying: a voice crying in the desert: prepare the way of the Lord — in this, that the order of the law and the prophets would cease from then on, through fulfillment, not destruction, and the kingdom of God would be announced by Christ — therefore, He more easily affirmed that the elements would pass away than His own words, confirming also what He had said about John, that it had not passed away.

choices.why: The Latin word 'mamona' is translated as 'wealth, riches' to convey the idea of material possessions.
The Latin word 'deus' is translated as 'God' to refer to the supreme being.
The Latin word 'creator' is translated as 'creator' to refer to the one who created the world.

bible_refs.note: You cannot serve God and mammon
A voice crying in the desert: prepare the way of the Lord

pass_b_english: Jesus says two masters cannot be served, because you must offend one to defend the other. He identifies them: God and mammon. You want to know what mammon means? If you lack an interpreter, learn it from Jesus Himself. He warns us to secure our futures through worldly friendships, citing the shrewd manager who, once fired, slashed his master’s debtors’ bills to feather his own nest. ‘I tell you,’ Jesus says, ‘make friends for yourselves with the mammon of unrighteousness’ — that is, money, the very stuff that manager handled (Luke 16:13). Everyone knows money writes the rules and runs the world. When Jesus saw the Pharisees’ greed, He drove the point home: ‘You cannot serve God and mammon.’ The money-loving Pharisees sneered. They knew perfectly well He meant cash, not that some ‘creator’ was hidden in the word mammon, as if Christ had come to recall them from serving that creator.

So what now? Learn this instead: Christ reveals one God. He names two masters — God and mammon, the Creator and money — and says, ‘You cannot serve God’ — the One they claimed to serve — ‘and mammon,’ the one they actually served. If Jesus were some other god, He would have had to name three masters: the Creator (who is God, therefore the greater Lord, more binding on us), mammon, and Himself. But He called mammon a lord, paired it with the true Lord, and said nothing about the Creator? Would silence mean the Creator ‘may’ be served, just not alongside mammon? When He sets up one God, He names the Creator. If He were a second god, He just named the Creator as Lord — without any other god beside Him.

That clarifies the saying: ‘If you have not been faithful in the mammon of unrighteousness, who will entrust you with what is true?’ He means unjust money, not the Creator — whom even Marcion calls just. ‘If you have not been faithful in what belongs to another, who will give you what is yours?’ What is unjust must be alien to a half-god. But how was the Creator ‘alien’ to the Pharisees? He was the proper God of the Jewish nation. If these words target mammon, not the Creator, then ‘who will trust you with what is truer?’ and ‘who will give you what is mine?’ Jesus cannot speak as if the true riches belong to another god’s grace. That would only make sense if He had charged them with unfaithfulness to the Creator — invoking the Creator to distinguish His own god and keep the Creator’s unfaithful from receiving His truth.

The Pharisees justified themselves before men and banked their reward on human approval. Jesus hits them with the same logic as Jeremiah: ‘Cursed is the man who trusts in man.’ When He adds, ‘But God knows your hearts,’ He invokes the power of the God who declared Himself the searcher of kidneys and hearts. On pride: ‘What is exalted among men is an abomination to God.’ He holds up Isaiah: ‘The day of the Lord of hosts comes upon every arrogant and haughty one, upon everyone lifted high — and they will be humbled.’

I can now see why Marcion’s god stayed hidden so long. He was waiting, I suppose, until he had learned all this from the Creator. So he studied up to John’s time, then launched his kingdom announcement: ‘The Law and the Prophets until John; from him the kingdom of God is proclaimed.’ As if we don’t already recognize John as the dividing line between old and new — where Judaism stops and Christianity starts — not because a different power shut down the Law and opened the Gospel, but because the Creator Himself ordained the transition. If we have proven that the old passes and the new arrives by the Creator’s own prediction, and John is shown as the forerunner preparing the Lord’s way, and the Gospel brings and proclaims the kingdom of God, then once John appears, Christ must be the One who follows John as forerunner. If the old ended and the new began with John in between, it’s no surprise — it’s the Creator’s design, proved more decisively by the Law and Prophets’ sunset in John and the kingdom’s dawn than by any other sign.

‘Heaven and earth will pass away sooner than one dot of the Lord’s words — for the word of our God stands forever’. Because in Isaiah, Christ — the Word and Spirit of the Creator — had already foretold John: ‘A voice crying in the wilderness: Prepare the way of the Lord’ (Isaiah 40:3). This meant the order of the Law and Prophets would cease from that point by fulfillment, not destruction, and the kingdom of God would be announced by Christ. That is why He could more easily affirm that the elements will pass away than His own words, confirming that what He said about John would not pass away either.
